Hi Olga / Avery,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We'd like to lock in the POC kickoff and a hands-on working session focused on routing policy (model selection, fallback rules, regional routing, and tiering). Our engineering and platform teams will be hands-on — goal is prompt review + a short load test at the end.

Preferred windows (PST):
- May 10th afternoon (13:00–16:00)
- May 11th morning (09:00–12:00)
- May 12th any time (we can be flexible)

I've attached an updated agenda (POC_Agenda_v2.pdf) showing topics and proposed owners. Also: we'll need a short pre-check for network & egress rules from our infra team (I'll share contact details once time is set).

Attendees from Nimbus: Megan Li (platform lead), Alex Tang (SRE)

Thanks,
Megan

Avery, Stephanie — can you confirm capacity for May 10 afternoon or May 18 if Nimbus needs a later week? We should plan for a 3-hour hands-on block and a separate 60–90 minute kickoff for stakeholders.

Megan — good outline. A couple of operational notes from our side: 

- We'll allocate a 3-hour hands-on lab for model selection and routing policy configuration (recommended cadence: 90 mins prompt/review & routing, 60 mins load test, 30 mins wrap).
- For the load test we need a 15-min ramp and one 15-min steady state for ~100 concurrent prompt streams. Please confirm if that approximate concurrency is realistic on your end.
- Please run the attached network-checklist.txt with your SRE before the pre-call. It lists ports, domains, and a simple curl test to validate egress.

Proposed internal owners during the session:
- Model selection, quantization/cost tradeoffs: Avery Johnson (you can call out particular models in advance)
- Fallback & tiering policies: Olga Petrov
- Tracing & observability setup: Stephanie Nguyen

If Nimbus needs later dates, May 17/18 are open for me as a backup.

Attachments: network-checklist.txt (text/plain)

Thanks,
Avery
Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwood.com

Also: Alex from our infra asked whether Redwood can provide the region/endpoint list to pin for the test (we run in us-west and us-east; want to avoid cross-region egress during the load).
